name: Skip-Bo
title: Skip-Bo Score Sheet – Free Printable PDF & Scorekeeper
description: Free printable Skip-Bo score sheet for playing to 500 points, with the scoring rules, in three PDF versions, plus an online scorekeeper.

columns: When a player empties their stockpile
rows: Each card left in an opponent's stockpile

content.intro: Print a Skip-Bo score sheet for playing to 500, or keep score on your phone. One hand is quick; a game to 500 takes an evening, and the sheet keeps track.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column. A hand ends when one player plays the last card from their stockpile. That player wins the hand and is the only one who scores.
The winner scores 25 points, plus 5 points for every card still in the other players' stockpiles. Count those cards, work out the total and write it in the winner's column; leave the others empty.
Keep playing hands until someone reaches 500 points. Online, the sheet adds every hand and shows the winner as soon as someone passes 500. For a shorter game, just play one hand and skip the scoring.

howToPlay.heading: How a hand of Skip-Bo works
paragraphs: Each player is dealt a stockpile, 30 cards for two to four players or 20 for five or six, and turns its top card face up. The rest of the deck is the draw pile. In the middle of the table are up to four shared building piles, which always start with a 1 and go up in order to 12.

At the start of each turn you draw until you hold five cards. Then you play as many cards as you can onto the building piles, from your hand, the top of your stockpile or the tops of your four discard piles. Skip-Bo cards are wild and can be any number. Your turn ends when you place one card from your hand on one of your own discard piles.

The top card of your stockpile is the one that matters, because the first player to play their whole stockpile wins the hand. Playing it whenever you can, and holding back cards the next player needs for their stockpile, is most of the strategy. If you empty your hand during a turn, draw five more and keep playing.

tips: Count only the cards left in each opponent's stockpile. Cards in their hands and discard piles are worth nothing.
Many families play a single hand and skip the scoring. Use the sheet when you want a longer game in which a big win counts for more.
For a shorter scored game, deal 20-card stockpiles to everyone or play to 250. The points work the same way.
If the draw pile runs out, shuffle the completed building piles into a new one. The hand carries on and the scoring does not change.

faqs.a: The player who empties their stockpile first wins the hand and scores 25 points, plus 5 points for each card left in their opponents' stockpiles. The other players score nothing that hand.

faqs.q: How many points do you need to win Skip-Bo?
faqs.a: 500. Players keep playing hands until someone's total reaches 500. Many families play a single hand instead, and the first to empty their stockpile wins.

faqs.q: How many cards are in each stockpile?
faqs.a: 30 cards each for two to four players, and 20 cards each for five or six players.
Skip-Bo cards are wild. They can be played as any number on a building pile.

faqs.q: What happens when a building pile reaches 12?
faqs.a: The completed pile is set aside and shuffled back into the draw pile when it runs out, and a new building pile can be started with a 1 or a Skip-Bo card.

faqs.q: How many people can play Skip-Bo?
faqs.a: Two to six players, or six in teams of two. The printable sheet and the online scorekeeper both have room for six.
